cohort: The study included 295 obese women (BMI > 30 kg/m2) and 590 normal-weight women (BMI 18.5-24.9 kg/m2) in Conakry, Guinea.
finding: Maternal obesity in low-income settings is associated with significantly increased risks of adverse labor, delivery, and perinatal outcomes, similar to findings in higher-resource contexts.
mod_finding: Obese parturients had increased rates of episiotomy (RR = 2.5), vacuum-assisted delivery (RR = 1.9), and cesarean section (RR = 1.7) compared to normal-weight women.
